---
name: "Academic Productivity"
description: "Connects academic productivity blockers to concrete strategies, assistive technologies and tools."
categories: [content-distribution, web-app, built-by-ai, powered-by-ai]
updated: 2026-07-16
deployments:
  Appsite:
    "Academic Productivity": https://academicproductivity.edutools.fyi/
---
# Academic Productivity Hub

A comprehensive interactive resource for academic productivity strategies, assistive technologies, and digital tools. This application helps users understand productivity blockers, explore strategies to reduce cognitive load, and find appropriate hardware and software tools.

## Architecture

This project is a Single Page Application (SPA) built with modern frontend technologies, designed for performance and maintainability.

*   **Framework**: React 19 with TypeScript.
*   **Routing**: React Router DOM (utilizing `HashRouter` to ensure compatibility with static hosting environments).
*   **Styling**: Tailwind CSS (integrated via CDN for rapid styling without a complex build step in this environment).
*   **Icons**: Lucide React.
*   **AI Integration**: Google GenAI SDK (`@google/genai`) facilitates real-time data retrieval.

### Key Components

*   `App.tsx`: The application entry point managing the router configuration.
*   `components/Layout.tsx`: Provides the persistent shell (navigation, responsive menu, footer).
*   `components/ToolCard.tsx`: A sophisticated component that displays static tool data and implements an on-demand AI search feature. It uses the Gemini API to fetch real-time pricing, reviews, and updates.
*   `pages/`: Modular view components for each section (Strategies, Blockers, AssistiveTech, ToolsDatabase, Hardware).
*   `data/content.ts`: A structured data layer containing the static definitions for strategies and tools, typed strictly via TypeScript interfaces.

## AI Integration

The application leverages the **Gemini 2.5 Flash** model via the `@google/genai` SDK to enhance the static database with live web information.

### Feature: Live Tool Research
When a user requests "Current info" on a tool card:
1.  The app initializes the `GoogleGenAI` client with `process.env.API_KEY`.
2.  It constructs a prompt requesting current status, pricing, and reviews for the specific tool.
3.  It utilizes the `googleSearch` tool configuration to ensure the model has access to the latest web data.
4.  The response (including text and grounding metadata/sources) is parsed and rendered dynamically within the card.

## Deployment

The application is architected as a static site, making it suitable for deployment on any static hosting provider.

### Requirements
*   **API Key**: A valid Google GenAI API Key is required for the search functionality. The application expects this to be available at `process.env.API_KEY`.

### Hosting Options
Because the app uses `HashRouter`, it does not require server-side routing support (e.g., Nginx rewrite rules). It works out-of-the-box on:
*   GitHub Pages
*   Netlify
*   Vercel
*   AWS S3 / CloudFront

### Development
The project uses ES Modules directly in the browser via an `importmap` in `index.html`.
*   **Dependencies**: React, ReactDOM, React Router, Lucide, and the Google GenAI SDK are loaded from CDNs.
*   **TypeScript**: Ensures type safety across the data layer and component props.

import { Tool, Strategy } from '../types';

export const strategies: Strategy[] = [
  {
    id: 'Listen',
    title: 'Listen: Read with your ears',
    shortDescription: 'Listen instead of reading or while reading to improve concentration and comprehension.',
    fullDescription: 'Listening to text helps slower readers speed up, reduces eye strain, and improves understanding. It is also a powerful tool for proofreading your own writing to catch errors that eyes might skip over.',
    actionItems: [
      'Use Read Aloud in Microsoft Edge & Office.',
      'Listen to PDFs with Voice Dream Reader.',
      'Use text-to-speech for proofreading drafts.',
      'Crop headers/footers in PDFs for smoother listening.'
    ],
    iconName: 'Headphones'
  },
  {
    id: 'Enlarge',
    title: 'Enlarge: Speed up reading',
    shortDescription: 'Reduce visual clutter and increase font size to reduce cognitive load.',
    fullDescription: 'The smaller the font, the more effort is spent on decoding. Increasing font size, line spacing, and reducing line length can significantly speed up reading and reduce mental fatigue.',
    actionItems: [
      'Use Immersive Reader in Edge/OneNote.',
      'Reflow PDFs on mobile devices.',
      'Increase zoom level on browser pages.',
      'Use "Liquid Mode" in Adobe Acrobat.'
    ],
    iconName: 'ZoomIn'
  },
  {
    id: 'Outline',
    title: 'Outline and Navigate',
    shortDescription: 'See the bigger picture using outlines, navigation panes, and mind maps.',
    fullDescription: 'Understanding the structure of a text helps strategic reading. Using Heading Styles in Word allows for navigation, automatic table of contents, and better accessibility.',
    actionItems: [
      'Use the Navigation Pane in Word.',
      'Apply Heading Styles (H1, H2, H3) rigorously.',
      'Create mind maps to visualize complex concepts.',
      'Scan headings and lists before deep reading.'
    ],
    iconName: 'ListTree'
  },
  {
    id: 'Dictate',
    title: 'Dictate',
    shortDescription: 'Save your hands and improve spelling by speaking your text.',
    fullDescription: 'Dictation technology is now highly accurate and free. It reduces physical strain and helps formulate complex thoughts without the barrier of typing and spelling mechanics.',
    actionItems: [
      'Use Dictate in Microsoft Office (Alt + `).',
      'Use Windows Dictation (Win + H).',
      'Use Voice Typing in Google Docs.',
      'Speak in complete sentences and review by listening.'
    ],
    iconName: 'Mic'
  }
];

export const tools: Tool[] = [
  // Hardware - Laptops & General
  {
    id: 'laptop-generic',
    name: 'Modern Laptop',
    description: 'Any laptop from a reputable manufacturer (Dell, HP, Apple, etc.) capable of running assistive tech.',
    category: 'Hardware',
    cost: '£400 - £1200+',
    pros: ['General purpose', 'Essential for university', 'Runs full desktop software'],
    cons: ['Battery life varies', 'Can be heavy', 'Expensive'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline', 'Dictate', 'Enlarge']
  },
  // Hardware - Tablets/eReaders
  {
    id: 'ipad-pro',
    name: 'iPad Pro (12.9in)',
    description: 'Large tablet great for combining reading, writing, and taking notes by hand.',
    category: 'Hardware',
    cost: '£1000+',
    pros: ['Large screen for A4 PDFs', 'Powerful ecosystem', 'Great for creative work'],
    cons: ['Very expensive', 'Heavy', 'Screen glare', 'Battery life lower than eInk'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Enlarge', 'Listen']
  },
  {
    id: 'remarkable-2',
    name: 'reMarkable 2',
    description: 'Distraction-free eInk tablet for reading and handwriting.',
    category: 'eReader',
    cost: '£360 - £480',
    pros: ['Paper-like feel', 'No eye strain', 'Long battery life', 'Distraction free'],
    cons: ['No backlight', 'No apps/web browsing', 'Proprietary sync'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline']
  },
  {
    id: 'kobo-elipsa',
    name: 'Kobo Elipsa',
    description: 'eReader and note-taker with stylus and public library access.',
    category: 'eReader',
    cost: '£350',
    pros: ['Illuminated screen', 'Overdrive (Library) support', 'Cheaper than iPad'],
    cons: ['Plastic build', 'No app store', ' bulky case'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Enlarge']
  },
  {
    id: 'onyx-boox-lumi',
    name: 'Onyx Boox Max Lumi',
    description: 'Massive 13.3in eInk Android tablet suitable for A4 documents.',
    category: 'eReader',
    cost: '£800',
    pros: ['A4 size at 100%', 'Android Apps support', 'Can be external monitor'],
    cons: ['Very expensive', 'Niche product'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Enlarge', 'Listen']
  },
  // Hardware - Accessibility
  {
    id: 'c-pen-connect',
    name: 'C-Pen Connect',
    description: 'Digital highlighter that scans text to your phone/computer.',
    category: 'Accessibility',
    cost: '£120',
    pros: ['Scans directly to digital', 'Portable', 'Good OCR'],
    cons: ['Line-by-line scanning only', 'Requires connected device'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Listen']
  },
  {
    id: 'ruby-10',
    name: 'Ruby 10 Magnifier',
    description: 'Digital magnifier with text-to-speech for visually impaired users.',
    category: 'Accessibility',
    cost: '£1800',
    pros: ['High contrast', 'Tactile buttons', 'Read aloud function'],
    cons: ['Extremely expensive', 'Bulky'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Enlarge', 'Listen']
  },
  // Software - Note taking
  {
    id: 'onenote',
    name: 'Microsoft OneNote',
    description: 'Digital notebook supporting text, images, ink, and audio.',
    category: 'Note-taking',
    cost: 'Free',

    cons: ['Organization can get messy', 'Sync issues occasionally'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline', 'Dictate']

    id: 'notion',
    name: 'Notion',
    description: 'All-in-one workspace for notes, databases, and project management.',
    category: 'Note-taking',
    cost: 'Freemium',
    pros: ['Powerful databases', 'Flexible layout', 'Web publishing'],
    cons: ['No offline mode', 'Steep learning curve', 'No ink support'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline']

    id: 'obsidian',
    name: 'Obsidian',
    description: 'Knowledge base that works on top of a local folder of Markdown files.',
    category: 'Note-taking',
    cost: 'Free (Sync is paid)',
    pros: ['Local files', 'Graph view of connections', 'Extremely customizable'],
    cons: ['Requires learning Markdown', 'Sync is paid'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline']
  },
  // Software - Reference & Reading
  {
    id: 'zotero',
    name: 'Zotero',
    description: 'Free reference manager that helps collect, organize, cite, and share research.',
    category: 'Reference Manager',
    cost: 'Free',
    pros: ['Open source', 'Great web clipper', 'Integrated PDF reader'],
    cons: ['Storage limits for free tier', 'Dated UI'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline']
  },
  {
    id: 'voice-dream',
    name: 'Voice Dream Reader',
    description: 'Top-tier text-to-speech app for mobile devices.',
    category: 'PDF Reader',
    cost: '£25',
    pros: ['Best-in-class TTS', 'Visual customization', 'Works with many formats'],
    cons: ['Expensive for an app', 'No desktop version'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Listen', 'Enlarge']
  },
  {
    id: 'liquid-text',
    name: 'LiquidText',
    description: 'PDF reader for iPad focusing on connecting ideas and distinct excerpts.',
    category: 'PDF Reader',
    cost: 'Freemium',
    pros: ['Unique workspace UI', 'Great for connecting concepts'],
    cons: ['Expensive subscriptions', 'Non-standard interface'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Outline']
  },
  // Software - Native Features
  {
    id: 'immersive-reader',
    name: 'Immersive Reader',
    description: 'Microsoft tool to remove distractions and read text aloud.',
    category: 'Accessibility',
    cost: 'Free',
    pros: ['Built into Edge/Word', 'Grammar tools', 'Distraction free'],
    cons: ['Inconsistent across apps', 'Online required for some voices'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Listen', 'Enlarge']
  },
  {
    id: 'read-aloud',
    name: 'Read Aloud',
    description: 'Text-to-speech feature in Microsoft Edge and Office.',
    category: 'Accessibility',
    cost: 'Free',
    pros: ['Natural voices', 'Zero setup', 'Highlights text as it reads'],
    cons: ['Requires internet for best voices'],
    relatedStrategies: ['Listen']
  }
];

import React from 'react'; import { Brain, Users, Smile, Eye, Ear, Clock, Briefcase, Mail, Building, Activity } from 'lucide-react'; const Blockers: React.FC = () => { return (
{/* Introduction */}

Blockers to Productivity

Understanding the barriers to academic success and how to overcome them.

{/* Slide 8 */}

What do people need assistance with?

{/* Slide 9 */}

Reasons people need assistance

Cognition
  • Decoding (dyslexia)
  • Attention (ADHD)
  • Understanding (SLI)
Organisation
  • Cognitive (dyslexia, ADHD)
  • Task-based (dyslexia, ADHD)
  • Physical (dyspraxia)
Socialisation
  • Social cues (ASD)
  • Convention compliance
  • Extroversion/introversion
Emotion
  • Anxiety/depression
  • Sensitivity to stimuli
  • Sense of self worth
Perception
  • Accuity
  • Discrimination
  • Inner imagery
{/* Slide 10 - Venn Diagram Content */}

Neurodiversity Overlap

ADHD

Attention, Concentration, Planning, Regulating

Dyslexia

Words, Sounds, Memory, Sequencing

Dyspraxia (DCD)

Spatial Awareness, Motor-skills, Co-ordination

Autism Spectrum Disorders

Social skills, Sensitivity

Dyscalculia

Basic maths, Estimating numbers

SLI/LD (Center Intersection)

Understanding, Speaking

{/* Slide 11 */}

Everybody’s needs and difficulties are different

{/* Slide 12, 13, 14 - Perception */}

Perception blockers

SIGHT
HEARING

Perception has a hidden impact on cognition.

Perception impact on cognition

Slower processing
Working memory load
Limits organisation
{/* Slide 15 - Complexity */}

Neurodiversity is not straightforward

Permanent Situational Temporary
{/* Slide 16 - Microsoft Persona Spectrum */}

Microsoft Inclusive Design Principles

Sense Permanent Temporary Situational
Touch One arm Arm injury New parent
See Blind Cataract Distracted driver
Hear Deaf Ear infection Bartender
{/* Slide 17, 18 - Non-compliance */}

Many more dimensions, so we are really talking about non-compliance more than diversity.

Better distinction

Neuro-compliant

  • Can sit still for hours
  • Can focus without breaks
  • Can ignore noise

Neuro-non-compliant

  • Needs breaks
  • Needs to break activities into smaller chunks
  • Needs silence
{/* Slide 19 - Compliance is relative */}

Compliance is relative to structure not person

9:5 working day
Long narrative emails
Open plan offices
{/* Slide 20 - Everyone is dyslexic when... */}

Everyone is dyslexic when they are …

Busy
Tired
New
  • language
  • culture
  • environment
  • subject
); }; export default Blockers;

Hardware Decisions for Productive Study

Choosing the right hardware is crucial. It depends on your personal situation, study strategies (reading vs listening), and specific needs.

{/* Decision Matrix */}

Quick Comparison

Device Type Best For Trade-offs
Computers Writing, General Computing, heavy multitasking Not ideal for long reading, limited battery compared to tablets
Tablets Reading PDFs, annotating by hand, watching lectures More expensive for "Pro" features, screen glare
eReaders Distraction-free reading, outdoor reading Single purpose, often slow, black & white mostly
Phones Audiobooks, podcasts, quick capture Screen too small for serious academic reading
{/* Buying Advice */}

Laptop Requirements

  • RAM: 8GB minimum, 16GB highly recommended for multitasking.
  • Storage: 256GB SSD minimum. Avoid eMMC or HDD.
  • Screen: Touch screen is worth the extra expense for accessibility.
  • Platform: Mac is great but expensive. Windows offers better touch support.

Don't forget Accessories

  • Stylus: Essential for annotating on tablets.
  • Cases/Covers: Protect your investment.
  • Screen Covers: Matte/Paper-like covers reduce glare.
  • Ergonomics: Laptop stand and external keyboard for long sessions.

Visual Impairment Support

For students needing magnification, devices like the Ruby 10 or C-Pen scanners can be life-changing. However, many software features (like Immersive Reader) built into standard laptops now bridge this gap for free.

The Single Principle of Productivity

There is ultimately only one principle of academic productivity: decreasing cognitive load and increasing fluency.

The four "strategies" below are actually four distinct ways to reduce the cognitive load of reading and writing, freeing up your mental energy for understanding and insight.

Read more details at academicreading.edutools.fyi

How It Works

Cognitive Load Theory

By offloading decoding tasks (through text-to-speech) or visual processing (larger fonts), you reduce extraneous load, reserving working memory for intrinsic load (the actual content).

Fluency

Fluency is the ability to read or write with speed, accuracy, and proper expression. Tools like dictation and outlining remove mechanical friction, allowing thoughts to flow freely.

Accessibility is Productivity

Strategies originally designed for accessibility (like screen readers for visual impairment) turn out to be powerful productivity multipliers for all users by offering multi-modal engagement.

# Developing Competence: From Mental Maps to Fluent Performance

An interactive, AI-powered competency development application designed to help users assess skills, visualize progress, and generate personalized professional development plans based on the "Developing Competence" pedagogy.

## 🏗 Architecture

This application is built as a **Client-Side Single Page Application (SPA)** using React 19 and TypeScript. It operates entirely in the browser without a custom backend server, leveraging Google's Gemini API for dynamic content generation.

### Tech Stack
*   **Core**: React 19, ReactDOM 19
*   **Language**: TypeScript (ES Modules)
*   **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
*   **AI Engine**: Google Gemini API (`@google/genai` SDK)
*   **Visualization**: Recharts
*   **Icons**: Lucide React
*   **Module System**: Native Browser ES Modules (via Import Maps)

### Key Components

1.  **State Management (`App.tsx`)**
    *   Acts as the centralized store for the `competencyFramework` (structure), `assessment` (scores), and `plan` (text).
    *   Manages the "routing" between views (`AppView` enum).
    *   Ensures data persistence during the session as users switch between building, assessing, and planning.

2.  **Framework Builder (`components/FrameworkBuilder.tsx`)**
    *   **AI Integration**: Uses `gemini-2.5-flash` with JSON Schema output to generate structured competency frameworks (Areas -> Dimensions -> Levels) for any user-provided topic.
    *   Allows users to "Export" their custom frameworks as JSON files.

3.  **Assessment Engine (`components/AssessmentTool.tsx`)**
    *   Renders a dynamic form based on the currently loaded framework.
    *   **AI Integration**: Sends the user's scoring pattern to Gemini to generate a qualitative analysis of strengths and weaknesses.

4.  **Pedagogical Content (`components/TheoryViewer.tsx`)**
    *   Implements a custom "Course Mode" vs. "Scroll Mode" viewer.
    *   Renders semantic content blocks (Callouts, Tables, Lists) defined in `content/theory.ts`.

5.  **Analytics (`components/Dashboard.tsx`)**
    *   Visualizes competence coverage using Radar and Bar charts from `recharts`.
    *   Calculates the "Development Phase" metrics.

6.  **Planning Agent (`components/DevelopmentPlan.tsx`)**
    *   **AI Integration**: Acts as a professional development coach. It takes the structured assessment data and generates a JSON-structured plan (Goals, Strategy, Timeline) tailored to the specific "Conceptual vs. Procedural" learning model.

## 🧠 Theory of Operation

The app implements a specific pedagogical model:
1.  **Competence** is split into **Conceptual** (Mental Maps) and **Procedural** (Fluency).
2.  **Levels**: The framework strictly follows the Novice → Apprentice → Practitioner → Expert progression.
3.  **AI Agents**: The AI is prompted not just to "chat", but to act as an instructional designer, converting raw topics into this specific pedagogical structure.

## 🚀 Deployment

The application is static and uses an `importmap` in `index.html` to load dependencies from a CDN.

### Prerequisites
*   **Google Gemini API Key**: A valid API key is required to use the Generator, Assessment Analysis, and Planning features.

### Configuration
The application accesses the API key via `process.env.API_KEY`.
*   **Production**: Ensure your build environment or hosting provider injects this variable.
*   **Security Note**: As a client-side app, the API key is exposed in the browser network requests. For public production deployments, it is recommended to proxy these requests through a lightweight backend or use API key restrictions (referrer restrictions) in the Google AI Studio console.

### Directory Structure
```
/
├── index.html              # Entry point with Import Maps
├── index.tsx               # React Root
├── App.tsx                 # Main Logic & State
├── types.ts                # TypeScript Interfaces & Enums
├── data.ts                 # Static Theory Content
├── components/             # React UI Components
│   ├── FrameworkBuilder.tsx
│   ├── TheoryViewer.tsx
│   └── ...
└── content/                # Static Framework Data
```
